question: Does standardizing the route lane to 48/48/64 preserve the PARP1/BRAF route support that 32/24/32 produced?
why_it_must_be_measured_rather_than_assu: A beam search is not mathematically nested in its width. Intermediate pruning and the order in which candidates are expanded can both move when beam_width, expansion_width or realization_limit change, so a wider search is not guaranteed to contain a narrower one.
held_fixed: the cell and its docked root starting state
the production Fiber (delta from the contract, support compose_valid)
green_requires_all_of: C1 RECOVERY: for every cell, every eligible endpoint SMILES the narrow arm produced also appears in the wide arm's eligible set (wide is a superset of narrow)
C2 YIELD: for every cell, the wide arm's eligible endpoint count is greater than or equal to the narrow arm's
C3 CONTAINMENT IS REPORTED EXACTLY: the size and the members of narrow-minus-wide are published per cell whether or not they are empty
C4 COST: the wide arm's route-lane elapsed stays under 600 s per cell, which is a third of the 1800 s production proposal-worker bound
not_green_action: STOP and report. Do not select the other width to make it pass, and do not fall back to per-target widths without saying so explicitly; choosing a configuration after seeing a result is what this predeclaration exists to prevent.
scope_limit: This is a ROUND-ONE support comparison from each cell's docked root, not a campaign-outcome comparison. It cannot say which arm would win a docked campaign.

measured_before_sealing.executable_divergence_is_three_fields_no: beam_width, expansion_width and realization_limit. scale_balanced also differs in the contracts (None for parp1/braf, true for jak2/fa7/5ht1b) but NO production caller passes it to propose_route_expert_candidates, so every target already runs the function default False. It is declared-but-unconsumed on the production path.
